lanehyst_20260819.decision: Took the SECOND path, with one refinement: the hysteresis lands GATED behind a NEW id 'lanehyst' rather than as an edit to the promoted default. Folding it straight into lanesurv would silently change shipped turbo behavior for every bot with no way to A/B it; a new gate keeps the shipped decision byte-identical and makes the change measurable on its own.
lanehyst_20260819.why_not_the_anchor_path: No safe seam. bots/mode_retreat_generic.lua defines only GetDesire() -- it has NO Think(), so the ENGINE's built-in retreat owns all movement (fountain routing, TP home, shrine, escape items). lanehyst_20260819.rationale_c: Schmitt trigger on a blinking binary control signal. lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.defect: bots/mode_team_roam_generic.lua: the L1-TRADE and L5-COMBO branches bid RemapValClamped(hp,0,0.5,NONE,0.92) -- 0.92 chosen explicitly to outbid the PROMOTED lanesurv retreat at BOT_MODE_DESIRE_HIGH=0.75. lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.same_family_as: GH #29 (retreat guard chain priority inversion). The 0.92 literal was KEPT (not lowered to <=0.9): bidding just under a cap threshold is the same implicit coupling that produced this bug.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.shipped_default_impact: NONE. capmono_20260819.source: strategy work unit 2026-08-19T09:5xZ, the other half of GH #31 (director fixed the lane-kill side at 09:04Z by EXEMPTING those two branches; this covers the branches that stay capped)
capmono_20260819.defect: bots/mode_team_roam_generic.lua _divecap_CapForLanePush calls itself a 'soft ceiling' but implements a CLIFF: only desire > 0.9 is pulled down, and it lands at 0.72 -- BELOW the whole (0.72, 0.9] band that passes untouched. Every branch still routed through it bids RemapValClamped(J.GetHP(bot), 0, 0.5 or 0.6, BOT_MODE_DESIRE_NONE, 0.98) -- ConsiderHelpWhenCoreIsTargeted, ConsiderHelpAlly, J.ShouldPunishDive ('punish'), J.ShouldPunishOverchase ('overchase', ARMED in test_set.md). So the effective bid is NON-MONOTONIC in HP with its maximum at ~46% HP: full HP -> 0.72 (loses to the promoted lanesurv retreat at 0.75), 43% HP -> 0.843 (BEATS it), 36% HP -> 0.71 (loses again). The hero least able to survive a collapse is the only one who wins the desire auction and gets pinned into it -- and unlike the lane-kill branches, none of these four carries J.ShouldReleaseLaneCommit to escape.
capmono_20260819.change: Gated turbo + J.IsSoakCandidate('capmono'): inside the existing `if J.IsInLaningPhase() or J.IsPushing(hBot)` block, replace the cliff with a genuine ceiling, `if desire > 0.72 then return 0.72 end; return desire`. Off the gate the cliff line runs unchanged -- shipped defaults byte-for-byte identical. The GH #31 lane-kill exemption and the (still gated) 'divecap' collapse exemption both sit ABOVE this and are unaffected.
capmono_20260819.rationale_c: Two independent grounds. (1) Internal precedent: this is the same defect the director just fixed for l1trade/l5combo in GH #31 and the same shape as the wave13 dossier finding ('the old 0.95 bid outbid the PROMOTED lanesurv retreat (0.75) and pinned bots into losing trades'). (2) Standard strategy: commitment to a fight should rise with your ability to survive it, never fall -- a support at 43% HP collapsing HARDER than the same support at full HP is backwards under any Dota fight-commitment model. Monotonicity of an effective bid in HP is a shape property, not a tuning choice.
capmono_20260819.conservatism: The armed path can only ever LOWER a desire (pure min against the ceiling that is already there). That is why it is separable from 'divecap': divecap UNCAPS collapses during laning and was deliberately left dark because it could cause over-commitment; capmono cannot, by construction. One lever only -- the ceiling VALUE (0.72) is untouched.
capmono_20260819.validation: tests/test_capmono_ceiling.lua -- 12 cases on the real frame f_222428_lion_lich_burst (Lion 354/823 = 43.0% hp at t=314.0, Lich 660u + Axe 800u, no ally within 2200; ground truth from the replay: Lich dealt 436 damage, Lion died 6.9s later). Arming 'capmono' therefore changes shipped help-ally/help-core collapse behavior in the 44-55% HP band as well as the two punish ids; that breadth is deliberate (the defect is in the shared transform, not in any one branch) and is the main thing a batch read should watch.

tpdying_20260819.source: strategy work unit 2026-08-19T11:5xZ, backlog item 8 (the 'final bid reachability' sweep). First id audited from the group's untouched list: tpcommit. GH #35.
tpdying_20260819.defect: J.GetTpCommitDefendDesire pins a fresh TP responder in the answered lane's DEFEND mode with a 0.85 floor, and releases the pin on `J.GetHP(bot) < 0.40 or J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst(bot)`. The second clause is the ANTICIPATORY one -- the reason the release works at all, since a lander who waits for 40% has already eaten the burst -- but J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst hard-requires J.IsInLaningPhase() on its third line. The floor is only reachable from the two response-TP branches (J.GetRescueTpTarget / J.ShouldTpSupportTowerFight), which require level 6+ and a >3500u trip, so the frames it actually pins are overwhelmingly POST-laning. There the release degrades to the numeric clause alone: the pin holds until the lander is ALREADY losing. That is the same 'ground down in place' shape (wave12 dossier mechanism D, ~6/24 landing deaths) the release was written against, minus the half that made it work. Same family as GH #29 / #31 / #32: a condition whose DOMAIN does not cover its branch's domain.
tpdying_20260819.change: New pure predicate J.IsIncomingBurstLethal(bot, nWindow) -- the same mana/cd-aware estimator J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst runs over the enemies within 1100, without the laning gate; true when their castable burst already covers the bot's current health. Consumed by ONE new gated release clause inside J.GetTpCommitDefendDesire, immediately after the shipped release: `if J.IsSoakCandidate('tpdying') and J.IsIncomingBurstLethal(bot, 3.0) then release end`. Reachable only inside the existing 'tpcommit' gate, so both shipped play AND today's armed-tpcommit behavior are byte-identical until 'tpdying' is armed.
tpdying_20260819.rationale_c: Two grounds. (1) Internal: the shipped release's own comment states the contract -- '丢失了动手机会才会走', a lander who is dying has lost the chance. This restores that contract in the domain the floor runs in; nothing new is claimed. (2) Standard strategy: whether to hold a contested spot is decided on incoming damage vs effective HP, not on a fixed HP percentage -- a 100% HP support inside a lethal combo should leave, a 45% HP hero out of range should not. Anticipating burst rather than reacting to an HP threshold is the same principle the PROMOTED lanesurv rule already ships on.
tpdying_20260819.conservatism: The armed path can only RELEASE a pin (return nil sooner) -- it can never raise or create one, and it cannot fire at all unless 'tpcommit' is armed too. Structurally it cannot add commitment, the same separability argument that let capmono ship ahead of divecap. One lever: the floor VALUE (0.85), the 12s window and the shipped release are all untouched.

Reverse assertion: the shipped release is still exactly the laning-only pair (39% releases, 41% does not), so the test self-reports as obsolete if anyone makes the shipped release domain-correct.

roamstale_20260819.defect: bots/mode_team_roam_generic.lua: the file-local `hTargetCreep` has exactly ONE writer -- the last-hit branch of GetDesireHelper -- which sits BELOW all six early-returning desire branches (X.ConsiderHelpWhenCoreIsTargeted [SHIPPED], ConsiderHelpAlly [SHIPPED], J.ShouldPunishDive ['ownhalf'], J.ShouldPunishOverchase ['overchase', armed], J.ShouldInitiateLaneKill ['l1trade'], J.ShouldSupportComboKill ['l5combo']), and it is never reset. So on every frame one of those six branches wins the desire auction, this mode's Think attacks LAST FRAME'S creep and never touches the collapse/commit target the desire was computed from. tparrive_20260819.defect: J.ShouldTpSupportTowerFight's winnability gate is structurally blind to the responder it is deciding for. The helper requires the responder be > 3500 from the threatened tower and picks its target from the enemies within 1200 of that tower; J.SafeToCommitFight scores only heroes within 1200 of that target. The responder is therefore at least 2300 units outside its own read (asserted on all three acceptance frames), so 'is this collapse winnable' is evaluated as though the TP never happens -- it actually asks 'is this fight already fine WITHOUT me'. The helper's own HEAT GATE makes the inversion systematic: the ally the count is sure to include is REQUIRED to be hurt or under hero fire. Net effect: the 1-ally-dived-by-2 collapse the fix exists for is refused (1 >= 2 false), while the 2v2 that needs nobody is allowed. Same family as GH #29/#31/#32/#34/#35/#37 (test_set.md 0b: the helper's reasoning quietly invalidated by the consumed mechanism), and it is the FIRST case where the invalidating mechanism is the CALLER'S OWN precondition rather than a downstream transform.

defstale_20260820.defect: aba_defend.DefendThink's bail-out -- the source's own comment calls it 'a small don't-walk-through-fire guard' -- reads `bot:WasRecentlyDamagedByAnyHero(5) and #pathEnemies > #ds.nInRangeEnemy`, i.e. 'more enemies on my PATH than IN RANGE'. Both sides are the SAME query, jmz.GetLastSeenEnemiesNearLoc(botLocation, 1600). `pathEnemies` is that query bucketed to 500ms on the bot handle; `ds.nInRangeEnemy` is that query written at the BOTTOM of GetDefendDesireHelper, below SEVEN early returns -- one of which (`#closeEnemiesDefend > 0 and #closeAlliesDefend >= #closeEnemiesDefend`) fires on exactly the frames DefendThink runs on, i.e. whenever a fight is happening within 900. bot._defend is never reset, so during a fight the right-hand side freezes at its pre-fight value, or at the initial empty table (0) if no call ever reached the bottom. The comparison is therefore bought entirely by staleness, never by a real path/range difference -- and when true the bot walks 700 back toward its fountain and returns, abandoning every other DefendThink branch for the frame.
defstale_20260820.family: Director's 0b family. Closest relative is roamstale (a state field written below early-returning bid branches and read first by Think), but the subtype is new: here the stale field is not a handle but a COUNT, and it is compared against a fresher copy of ITSELF, so the branch's stated meaning is unrepresentable rather than merely mis-targeted.

defstale_20260820.domain_measured: Over the 3 replays of the 22:25-22:36 wave, 1437 hero-frames have the shape 'under hero fire within 5s AND within 1600 of an own building AND >=1 enemy within 1600'. On a 45-frame sample of those, the guard's CONDITION is true on 32 (71%) -- 27 of them because nInRangeEnemy is still 0. Reachability is much narrower: a defend mode wins the SCRIPT auction on only 1 of those 45 (the pinned drow frame), because mode_retreat_generic usually outbids defend while a bot is under fire. On a separate 70-frame random sample, defend wins 26 times but never with the guard true. So this is a real, un-gated, wrong decision with a NARROW measured footprint -- and the footprint is a lower bound, since the engine's built-in modes have no script GetDesire (GH #27).

defstale_20260820.rationale_c: Two standard arguments. (1) Engineering: a decision must not be taken on a comparison of a quantity with an older copy of itself -- the branch cannot express what its own comment claims. (2) Play: in Turbo a tier-1/2 tower under a lone opponent is worth holding at 78% hp; giving up the frame to walk backwards forfeits the creep wave, the xp and the trade, and the honest 'am I losing this fight' judgement is already made twice elsewhere in the same file (#nInRangeEnemy > #nInRangeAlly at lines 1115 and 1172) and by mode_retreat_generic's own bid.

It was not taken this round because it adds firings in situations that have never been measured, and the charter's own lanefix lesson says ship one monotone lever at a time. Do it after defstale measures neutral-or-better, on a clean baseline.
